clauses.reason: Executive Order 10949, signed 1961-06-26, creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, directs it to report to the President "on or before" June 30, 1961, and provides that after its report the board continues in existence until "terminated by the President". Three commands result: creation of the board, the report deadline, and continued existence until presidential termination. Later event: Executive Order 10951, signed 1961-06-29, extends until 9 a.m., July 3, 1961 the time within which this board must report (inclusive reading; the exclusive reading is that it ends when that moment begins). The extension is a later event with its own quote, and an extended report deadline is not an end (owner rulings 2026-10-21 until-dates and report deadline). The only own-terms end is termination by the President. No held text records one: a held-corpus regular-expression search for a board of inquiry being terminated returned no match, and no held text gives the date the board reported. That absence is not proof that no termination occurred, so it is disclosed as an open earlier-end candidate; the held evidence does not show an earlier end, and under the owner’s report-deadline ruling the order ends on its express revocation. First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number; its enacting sentence (outside the cited span) revokes the listed orders and any amendments to them, and the cited span, page 12 of the held text, lists the order on its own row, "10949 Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the maritime industry", beginning at character offset 16156; the same table lists EO 10951, the amendment. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
EO 10949 creates the Taft-Hartley Board of Inquiry for the 1961 maritime dispute; provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed identity, and confirmed a single-clause inventory. EO 10951 extended the report time (a later event). The own-terms contingent end (termination by the President) is not shown by held evidence and is disclosed. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) revokes the order and its amendment and is the first end in held evidence.

savings.reason: EO 12553 has no saving, exception or pending-matters language: a search of the whole held text for except, notwithstanding, nothing in, saving, pending and similar words found only incidental uses inside other orders’ subject lines. The board’s report and any later proceedings in the maritime dispute rest on the Labor-Management Relations Act and the parties’ acts, not on this order.
